title: Pillar of sunlight over ALMA
caption: A sun pillar over an ALMA antenna on the Chajnantor plateau, Chile
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Reds and blues fill the sky over the Chajnantor plateau in Chile's Atacama Desert, and a sun pillar rises from the Sun in line with a large antenna. Clouds are a rare sight in this dry region, and they help create the colorful display.

A sun pillar is an optical effect produced by ice crystals in the atmosphere. The antenna in the photograph belongs to the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array, or ALMA, which ESO co-owns. The Chajnantor plateau is its home.

ALMA is among the world's most powerful observatories for radio astronomy. It has a collection of 66 antennae, each one much like the antenna pictured, and the array has been responsible for many groundbreaking discoveries over the years. It also contributed to making the first image of a black hole.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph by C. Duran of an ALMA antenna under a cloudy sky. The source gives no camera or color details.
understand.eye: The colors and the sun pillar are ordinary visible light, but the antenna itself observes radio wavelengths that the eye cannot see.
